::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 9th 1873  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection C0171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Miss Medhurst](people/person_988.qmd)
I did hope to have put in [this sonnet](other_books/otherbook_835.qmd) of yours in time for Ascension day, but I could not manage it, so I can only send you the proof and thank you for your kindness to [Emmeline Spratt](people/person_1358.qmd), who after her visit to you wrote the happiest letter she had written at all since leaving home[^1]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: In fact the sonnet waited a year to be published in *MP* (May 1874).  Blanche Medhurst's social work had brought her in touch with Emmeline, the niece of CMY's maid Harriet Spratt.
